Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

bet noun and verb

also wager, bets, make a bet, win a bet, lose a bet, place a bet, stake, I bet you, betting

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.3.132: Apronium spōnsiōne lacessīvit (Lewis & Short)
Juv. 11.202: audāx spōnsiō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 94: tē spōnsiōne prōvocō, I bet you

spōnsiō, spōnsiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a bet, a wager

In Roman law a wager on the outcome of a case, the loser to pay a sum (Lewis & Short); of betting in general from Juvenal on. To bet someone, aliquem spōnsiōne prōvocāre or lacessere; to win a bet, spōnsiōne vincere (Cic. Quinct. 84). Its first sense is a solemn promise, a guarantee (see guarantee).

Other words

  • pignus, pignoris n. — a stake, what is wagered

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 3.31: quō pignore certēs

    A pledge or security (Lewis & Short); in Vergil’s singing match, the stake: pignore certāre, to compete for a stake, to bet.

  • dēpōnō, dēpōnere, dēposuī, dēpositum — stake, lay as a wager

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. Ecl. 3.31–32: Ego hanc vitulam … dēpōnō (Lewis & Short)

    Its usual sense is to lay down, put aside, deposit (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • tū dīc mēcum quō pignore certēs

    you tell me what you will stake against meVerg. Ecl. 3.31

  • Tē spōnsiōne prōvocō illum nōn esse victūrum.

    I bet you he won’t win.Traupman 94

See also guarantee, sure, win, game.
